# hermes-on-Apple-container — live-prototype verdict (2026-07-15)

Supersedes the 2026-07-14 spike memo (note 452679f). Executes the 5-experiment matrix from backlog task 89dbaae on the live host (apple/container 1.1.0 + socktainer 1.1.1 installed with user approval). Full chronology + artifacts: cc-notes log `apple-container-prototype` (carries the verified proxy-fix diff as an attachment).

**Verdict: still NO-GO for immediate production, but the blockers narrowed sharply. The prototype turned "unknown, prototype-able" into "sandbox proven (with one small, verified proxy fix); memory/backup favorable; egress isolable but NOT free; the SINGLE remaining architectural blocker is lifecycle/recovery (#158/#286 — no boot-autostart, no restart policy)."** That blocker is upstream-tracked and buildable-around, not fundamental.

## Conjunctive gate table

| Gate | Verdict | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| **Sandbox path** | ✅ **CONDITIONAL PASS** | proxy→socktainer→apiserver→micro-VM: all 14 allowlisted routes work; 9 host-escape create-bodies 403'd. **BUT** the codex refuter found a CRITICAL host-escape (below); it is **fixed + verified**. Holds only WITH the fix. |
| **Egress isolation** | ⚠️ **PARTIAL — needs enforcement** | Fleet (metal/hermes/bluebubbles) unreachable on BOTH their vmnet 192.168.64.x AND their tailscale 100.x IPs; host gateway/LAN unreachable. **BUT a DEFAULT-network container CAN reach the host's OWN tailnet-bound services** (rapid-mlx 100.88.252.58:8000, mlx-audio :8765) + the internet (NAT). A **CUSTOM (non-NAT) network container reached NOTHING** — full isolation. So egress is isolable but not automatic. |
| **Recovery / lifecycle** | ❌ **FAIL as-is / achievable-with-work** | NO component auto-restarts (apiserver #158; socktainer + proxy unsupervised) — the standing blocker. Recovery needs a KeepAlive supervision layer (the fleet's `write_agent` pattern already exists). Cold-boot leg deferred (no-reboot constraint). |
| **Memory** | ✅ **PARTIAL PASS** | ~340 MB RSS per idle micro-VM (our measurement; the unsourced ~200 MB was low). A 2G machine holds only ~356 MB idle — NO pre-wiring, favorable vs tart's full 4 GiB. No-release-shrink + 24h growth: deferred (measurement contamination + time). |
| **Backup** | ✅ **PASS** | Bind-mount host paths keep the current restic file-level model (files appear directly on host). Named volumes are opaque ext4 images → migration MUST bind-mount hermes state, never named volumes. |
| *(bonus)* **Wholesale NixOS-in-a-machine** | ⚠️ **boot-blocked** | Not gate-critical (sandbox gate met by the socktainer path). Apple machine rootfs is read-only; NixOS's `/etc/resolv.conf` symlink into `/nix/store` fails Apple's `configureDns`. A scoped image-fix (writable `/etc` overlay) was attempted; needs real image engineering. |

## The critical finding (why the adversarial pass mattered)
socktainer transparently relays a container-internal `/var/run/docker.sock` **target** to its own raw, unfiltered API — regardless of mount source (relay is `docker.sock`-basename-specific; `containerd.sock`/`dockerd.sock`/`docker.sock.bak` are NOT relayed — verified). hermes-docker-proxy screens bind/mount **sources** but never **destinations**. Exploit run end-to-end THROUGH the proxy: `docker run -v <bindroot>/empty:/var/run/docker.sock` (passes screening) → inside, that path is a live socktainer socket → `docker run --privileged -v /:/hostroot` mounted the **HOST filesystem** (read `/Users/yasyf` = sops key + vault token). Full proxy bypass → host compromise. **Fixed**: a `forbiddenDest()` destination screen (blocks any bind/mount whose target basename is `docker.sock`) — verified to 403 the exploit (both `-v` and `--mount`), leave legit binds working, keep existing tests green, and the relay is basename-specific so the fix is complete. Diff attached to the log; backlog task da1c63 to port it. (Not currently exploitable on the live dockerd proxy — dockerd has no relay — but a hard socktainer-migration prerequisite and cheap defense-in-depth now.)

## Egress — corrected detail (the memo's concern was valid, via a different path)
Cross-vmnet isolation is strong: no container reached the fleet's 192.168.64.x, and the host gateway/LAN (192.168.4.24) is closed. The container also cannot reach OTHER tailnet peers (metal 100.64.60.1, hermes 100.95.192.38 — all closed; the host does not forward container→tailnet-peer traffic). The leak is narrow but real: a container on the **NAT'd default network** reaches the **host's own** tailnet-IP services (rapid-mlx/mlx-audio) and the open internet, because it NATs through the host. A **custom `container network create` network is NOT NAT'd and reached nothing at all**. Mitigation is straightforward and should be a migration requirement: run the nested code-exec sandboxes on a **custom non-NAT network** (zero egress), and give hermes-the-agent a controlled network + pf/tailscale-only egress (it needs tailscale to reach metal, since the fleet is unreachable via vmnet). IPv6 egress was blocked.

## Production prerequisites the migration must satisfy (conjunctive)
1. **Proxy destination-screening** (task da1c63) — REQUIRED; ready fix verified.
2. **Lifecycle supervision** — a KeepAlive/boot-autostart wrapper for apiserver + socktainer + proxy + the agent machine (mirrors the tart `write_agent` stack). The one architectural build item; upstream #158/#286 would obviate it.
3. **Egress enforcement** — code-exec sandboxes on a custom non-NAT network (verified zero-egress); hermes-the-agent on a controlled network with pf/tailscale-only egress (block the default-NAT internet + host tailnet-IP reach).
4. **tailscale in-container** — userspace-networking mode (proven to start; no caps needed); the agent reaches metal over the tailnet since the fleet is unreachable via vmnet. Full join+reach-metal test pending an ephemeral tag:hermes key.
5. **Bind-mount state** (not named volumes) so restic keeps working.
6. **Drop `--runtime runsc`** from the agent's docker args (socktainer ignores it; the per-VM boundary replaces gVisor — a STRONGER boundary).
7. Optional: the wholesale-NixOS-machine path if the "keep systemd+dockerd+proxy intact" route is preferred over rebuilding hermes as OCI containers — needs the read-only-rootfs image work.

## What's proven vs still open
PROVEN: sandbox filtering (with fix), fleet+host-gateway isolation, per-VM memory footprint, restic-compatible bind-mount backup, tailscale userspace mechanism, custom-network zero-egress, subnet-collision avoidance (192.168.72/24 override).
OPEN (deferred, not blocking the verdict): 24h memory soak + no-release quantification; cold-boot recovery (no-reboot constraint); full tailnet join (user authkey); the actual pf enforcement (root-gated); the wholesale-NixOS boot; the create-body field audit (VM-isolated, low risk).

## Re-evaluation triggers (standing watch — task ad1beb, log has the one-command check)
apple/container #158 (boot autostart) or #286 (restart policy) closing removes the lifecycle blocker → strong GO signal. Also: #66 Docker-API reversal, a first-party egress primitive, ballooning completion, new container/socktainer releases.
